data.cultural_impact: Krishna is a popular Hindu deity and is one of the most widely revered figures in Indian culture. He is also a central character in the two major Sanskrit epics: the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Krishna comes from the Sanskrit word 'Krsna', meaning 'black' or 'dark', and is also interpreted as 'all-attractive' or 'the best of all'. It signifies the ultimate cosmic consciousness and the inner divinity of the soul searching for its union with 'Brahmam', the supreme reality.

historical_references.reference: Jivitesh is a rare name in Hindu mythology and is believed to mean 'one who preserves life'. It is mentioned in the epic Mahabharata in the context of the great battle of Kurukshetra, where Jivitesh was an important divine charioteer of the great warrior Bhishma. He was tasked with preserving Bhishma's life even after he had been struck down in the battle.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata, Great Battle of Kurukshetra, Charioteer of Bhishma

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Jivitesh can be found in the Puranas, specifically the Bhagavata Purana. In this context, Jivitesh is mentioned as an avatar of Lord Vishnu, who appeared to protect the Devas (gods) from the demon Jalandhar. Jivitesh is described as a powerful warrior and is said to have killed Jalandhar, thus preserving the Devas' lives.
